Here, the Abhidhammas in the alphabetical form of Udaharun, which are issued in alphabetical order, are the opening words of Abhivatha, 2.233. I"m not sure if I"m going to be able to do that. Abhihate-hu Dantajata is found in Pratisana, Hta, 1.77, and Abhiha-te, only in Abhidha, in 2.62, is called Muddhazatha. In particular, in Abhidha, 2.233, there is Abhihate-hu Dantajata, and in that 62 book, there is Abhihate-hu Muddhazata, and it is a kind of front and back. The conversion of the Dantaja alphabet to the Muddhaza alphabet is generally performed only on the later elements of the water which are either watery or watery. Since the elements of these Abhidhammas are pure Hana-elements, there is no water, no water, and there is no reason for the later Dantajata-substance to be transferred to Muddha-jata. However, the translation of the existing text, which is considered to be the original Abhihata with Dantajata, is as follows: being beaten and tortured (a)being beaten, tortured and injured.(b) being killed and torture. (c)  being fought and tortured. (d) being beaten and tortured. see Abhihattapatta - see also Abhihata.

[Abhi+vagga] (pu) CL=7 Vagī-Saṃ. block-prohibit-expel-drive; one. Mass of inanimate and inanimate objects. William. Courage, power. William, Kotthubha.  Abhivagga is probably a military weapon. In the case of weapons, it is not a light weapon that can be moved, but a heavy weapon that can be mounted somewhere. According to the explanations of commentary and sub-commentary, after it is hooked with sharp edges at the base teeth at the base and lifted up by a machine and set up the trigger,  then dropped to torture and crush the enemy.  One might wonder if it was a weapon named 'Tone Maung' of the military weapons used in Eastern countries such as Burma. Because in the chapter about the battle in which Myanmar army besieged the Capital, Yodaya, in Konbaung Era Maha Rāzawindawgyi Vol.1 Page 402, it reads 'they did not come to fight but the defended the city firmly after poising the mortar and cannon and setting the catapult, Tone Maung.
In its chapter in the Konbaung Era Maha Rāzawindawgyi Vol.1 Page 458  about the battle in which the Chinese besieged Bala Min Htin stronghold, it reads ' Bala Min Htin too having mounted the cannon and mortar at the front of the city, set up Tone Maung, shot and stroke with the machine.] A collection of very heavy logs that are set up towards sth; Very powerful weapons; Tone Maung weapon ¿.
